meta.scope: Human epidural SCS ECAP measurements with a possible patient-linked clinical pain outcome
meta.rule: A publication, trial registry entry, or data-sharing promise does not establish access to a patient-linked analysis table or raw ECAP signals. Do not select a primary dataset until the owner confirms exact fields, linkage, and delivery route, and the responsible institution and legal/consent review separately establish permission for the proposed secondary use.

apm_registry_results_recheck_2026_09_28.verified: Official v2 record: overallStatus=COMPLETED, actual enrollment=30, results first posted 2026-09-25 and ipdSharing=NO. The posted primary outcome 'Succsessful Use of APM' reports 134 successful closed-loop program generations among 140 initiated APM uses (96%). The denominator is APM uses, not participants; the endpoint is programming workflow success, not pain relief or functional improvement.
apm_registry_results_recheck_2026_09_28.boundary: Posted aggregate results and study documents do not release participant-level ECAP and pain/function outcomes or grant independent reuse. This is a new audit observation of a 2026-09-25 registry post, not a new registry update after 2026-09-27. RES-04/05 remain open and STOP-H3-A remains in force.

pooled_dose_response_supplement_recheck_.publication: PMID 38508591, DOI 10.1136/rapm-2024-105346, PMC12015077; separate pooled dose-response analysis, not the NCT04319887 study article
pooled_dose_response_supplement_recheck_.verified: The primary JATS Data availability statement says data are available on reasonable request. The public supplementary ZIP has exactly two DOCX files (analysis methods and one figure description) plus eight figure images. Methods describe one selected maximum-analgesic-effect visit per patient, with physiological data from the preceding week; the fit-function check uses 2048 activation plots. No downloadable row-level patient key, ECAP waveform/feature table, pain-outcome table or reuse license was present in this bounded archive review.
pooled_dose_response_supplement_recheck_.boundary: The published analysis implies within-study patient linkage, but neither its public supplement nor its request-only statement grants this project an accessible linked dataset. Do not infer absence of underlying owner-held records or a usable independent secondary-analysis right.

pooled_nsrpb_subgroup_recheck_2026_09_27.publication: Hunter et al., Spine 2025, DOI 10.1097/BRS.0000000000005445, PMCID PMC12594148; post hoc NSRBP subgroup analysis of the EVOKE and ECAP trials
pooled_nsrpb_subgroup_recheck_2026_09_27.verified: Abstract Materials and Methods reports 68 NSRBP patients; Table 1 separates EVOKE N=26 and ECAP N=42. The paper reports aggregate pain and device metrics, but the checked full-text page has no downloadable participant-level ECAP/pain table or explicit data-availability/reuse statement. Both registry IPD-sharing fields are NO. NCT02924129 posts aggregate pain outcomes; NCT04319887 posts one aggregate ECAP result while six registered pain/function outcomes are NOT_POSTED in its results module.
pooled_nsrpb_subgroup_recheck_2026_09_27.boundary: The pooled analysis links two trial-source groups at study level; it does not provide this project with patient-linked ECAP and pain records, reuse permission or proof of cross-trial participant identity. The article's CC BY license covers its published text, not access to underlying patient data. Separate study articles' request policies do not establish access to this pooled-analysis dataset. RES-04/05 remain open.

screened_open_near_matches_2026_09_27.name: Sagalajev et al. 2024, acute SCS frequency, ECAP and paresthesia observation
screened_open_near_matches_2026_09_27.locator: Author-hosted journal PDF https://prescottlab.ca/images/pdf/2023Sagalajev.pdf, Fig. 1A and Results > Dependence of paresthesia on SCS frequency and its correlation with ECAP amplitude: one chronic-pain patient in an SCS trial, 150 Hz versus 1 kHz at the same 9.6 mA pulse setting, with paresthesia and detected ECAP only at 150 Hz. STAR Methods > Experimental Model and Subject Details and Human ECAP recordings confirm one patient, bipolar 8 mm electrode spacing, visually verified 50 μs/phase pulse width, and recordings during at least 10 min per condition. Text extraction rendered the micro sign as m; the visual PDF resolves the unit. Data and code availability: electrophysiology data on reasonable request, public modeling code at Zenodo 10019046 and ModelDB 267768. Official supplement https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S0896627323008024-mmc1.pdf has no released longitudinal participant table. Direct publisher fetch returned an access challenge, but the author-hosted complete journal PDF was independently reviewed on 2026-09-27.
screened_open_near_matches_2026_09_27.exclusion_reason: This is an acute ECAP-versus-stimulation-sensation comparison in one person, not longitudinal clinical pain relief or a reusable patient-linked ECAP-to-outcome dataset. It is relevant physiological prior art; no treatment-effect or clinical prediction claim is inferred.
